stimulus.body: 次の語について考えましょう：the torii gate。

questions.stem: Which claim about the torii gate is NOT correct? (鳥居)

options.text: A torii marks the boundary between the secular world and a Shinto sacred space.
options.misconception: confuses which of these claims about the torii gate is actually accurate

options.text: A torii is a wooden fence used to protect crops.
A torii is the main gate of a Buddhist monastery only.
options.misconception: confuses which of these claims about the torii gate is actually accurate

options.text: A torii is a ceremonial umbrella carried in processions.
options.misconception: confuses which of these claims about the torii gate is actually accurate

questions.explanation: The statement identified as NOT correct is inaccurate because A torii is a wooden fence used to protect crops.. By contrast, the accurate claim about the torii gate is: A torii marks the boundary between the secular world and a Shinto sacred space. Torii gates stand at shrine entrances, signaling passage into the precincts of the kami, and are often painted vermilion. Distinguishing a true description from a plausible false one is the point of this item.
questions.hint: Recall the established facts about the torii gate before judging each claim.

stimulus.body: 次の語について考えましょう：the Edo period。

questions.stem: Which statement about the Edo period is correct? (江戸時代)

options.text: The Edo period was a time of relative peace, urban growth, and flourishing popular culture under the Tokugawa shogunate.
The Edo period occurred before the introduction of rice cultivation to Japan.
options.misconception: introduces an inaccurate claim about the Edo period

options.text: The Edo period was a century of constant civil war and famine with no cultural achievements.
options.misconception: introduces an inaccurate claim about the Edo period

options.text: The Edo period saw Japan annexed by a foreign power.
options.misconception: introduces an inaccurate claim about the Edo period

questions.explanation: The accurate statement about the Edo period is: The Edo period was a time of relative peace, urban growth, and flourishing popular culture under the Tokugawa shogunate. During the Edo period, Tokugawa rule brought stability, the rise of cities like Edo, and the flowering of ukiyo-e, kabuki, and haiku. The other options distort the topic, which is why careful attention to what is actually asserted matters.
questions.hint: Recall the established facts about the Edo period before judging each claim.

questions.stem: The seminar leader reviews the prompt given below during a self-study session. In a short dialogue exercise, a question checks what the speaker says or does. Which statement about haiku is correct? (俳句)

options.text: Haiku must be written in the Japanese kanji script only.
options.misconception: introduces an inaccurate claim about haiku

options.text: Haiku always deals exclusively with political themes.
options.misconception: introduces an inaccurate claim about haiku

options.text: Haiku is a long narrative poem of several hundred lines.
options.misconception: introduces an inaccurate claim about haiku

options.text: Haiku is a short poem form conventionally structured with a 5-7-5 sound-unit pattern and a seasonal word.

questions.explanation: The accurate statement about haiku is: Haiku is a short poem form conventionally structured with a 5-7-5 sound-unit pattern and a seasonal word. Haiku uses a kigo, or seasonal reference, and a cutting word; Basho is among its most celebrated practitioners. The other options distort the topic, which is why careful attention to what is actually asserted matters.
